tob-10455: Kabir was a fifteenth-century Indian weaver-poet whose songs mocked the rituals of both Hindus and Muslims while celebrating a direct, loving experience of God. His verses — spare, earthy, and unforgettable — speak of the divine as an intimate presence beyond all temples and mosques. Rabindranath Tagore’s English renderings helped carry Kabir’s voice to the wider world.
tob-11055: Rudolf Steiner’s handbook promises a practical path to spiritual perception — exercises in concentration, meditation, and moral development meant to awaken ‘higher’ faculties of the soul. Written for beginners in his Anthroposophical movement, it lays out the inner training behind his teachings. The book became the standard manual for students of Steiner’s esoteric philosophy.
tob-4055: Anthropogenesis, the second volume of the Secret Doctrine, tells Blavatsky’s odd history of mankind — seven root races unfolding over ages, from airy spirit-forms to modern man. Atlantis and Lemuria loom large in her tale. Fanciful or not, it moved a whole crop of writers, painters, and seekers.
tob-13155: Legge’s Analects give the Master’s sayings in the great China-scholar’s careful English — his talks with learners on worth, study, and rule. Drawn from the Chinese Classics, this choice distills the teaching that shaped the East. The Analects stay the most quoted book in Chinese story.
tob-4155: Anna Kingsford and Edward Maitland’s Perfect Way sets forth their Christ-mystery — ‘the finding of Christ’ by hidden reading of writ. Kingsford, trail-blazing woman leech and seeress, claimed heaven’s warrant for their word. The book grew a classic of Victorian wonder-godliness.
tob-4255: Newbell Puckett’s Southland Black Beliefs — 1926 — is the trail-book on black American folk-faith, spell-work, and old wives’ tales. His field-gleanings set down conjure, haunts, and church-life at large. The book founded black folk-belief study. A landmark of American folk-lore.
tob-13455: The Liezi is the Tao-way classic laid to Lie Yukou — tales and teachings of the wise man, on unforcedness, dreams, and the Way. This olden text stands beside the Tao Te Ching and Chuang Tzu. The book is a treasure of early Tao thought.
arxiv-2605-09055: AI agents that need to touch real hardware — GPUs, sensors — face a discovery problem: what is plugged in and how is it controlled? Quilee Simeon, Justin M. Wei, and Yile Fan propose the Octopus Protocol: one-shot hardware discovery and control via infrastructure-as-prompts. The 2026 paper gives agents a standard handshake for the physical world.
arxiv-2605-09155: Every algebraic curve has a Jacobian — a geometric object encoding its secrets — and generalized versions stretch the concept further. Benjamin Castle, Ishai Dan-Cohen, and Assaf Hasson study a curve and its abstract generalized Jacobian. The 2026 paper is algebraic geometry on curves and their shadows.
arxiv-2605-09755: The power method finds dominant eigenvectors slowly; randomized sketching can speed it up dramatically. Shabarish Chenakkod and Michał Dereziński accelerate the power method with fast sketching for stronger low-rank approximation. The 2026 paper is fast, practical randomized numerical linear algebra.
arxiv-2605-09955: Subjective NLP tasks split annotators along real perspectival lines; majority voting erases the meaningful disagreement. Tadesse Destaw Belay, Ibrahim Said Ahmad, Idris Abdulmumin, and colleagues cluster by agreement instead. The 2026 paper models annotator perspectives beyond the majority. It honors disagreement instead of averaging it away.
arxiv-2605-10155: Legal assistance powered by AI — a multi-agent architecture with retrieval-augmented generation: NyayaAI. Deepanshu, Divi Saxena, Deepali Rana, and colleagues build the assistant. The 2026 paper is legal AI with teamwork. It assists busy lawyers with cooperating, retrieving agents daily.
arxiv-2605-10255: Qubit versus qudit encodings for EV charging and trip assignment problems — compared head to head. Linus Ekstrøm, Hao Wang, and Sebastian Schmitt run the comparison. The 2026 paper is quantum optimization. It charges EVs smartly with quantum bits and dits.
arxiv-2605-10555: Enterprise service interfaces rethought for LLM-native execution — agent-first tool APIs instead of human-first endpoints. Kai Pan and Rong Hou propose the redesign. The 2026 paper is enterprise AI architecture. It puts AI agents first when designing the interface.
pmc-13468655: Wheat grain protein content — stable QTLs identified and KASP markers developed from a Linmai2/Zhong892 recombinant inbred population. Nannan Zhao, Yamei Wang, Yuxuan Song, and colleagues do the breeding genetics. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is crop science. It gives breeders DNA markers for protein-rich wheat.

pmc-13420355: Posterior hip cysts resected during hip arthroscopy — through a posterolateral portal. Peng Chen, Yueyang Tian, Jiang Guo, and colleagues perform the resections. pmc-13519855: Adults with ischemic stroke — retinal microvascular and neuroretinal measures derived from optical coherence tomography and angiography. pmc-13518855: Free heme — scavenged by scavenger receptor BI, essential for protection against hemolysis. Misa Ito, Jianyao Xue, Ling Guo, and colleagues identify the receptor. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is heme biology. It finds the receptor mopping up spilled heme. Hemolysis, prevented.
pmc-13454355: MicrobeQuest! — an edugame evaluated for user enjoyment, engagement, and intention to play. Andreea Molnar and Patty Kostkova run the evaluation. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is educational game research. It tests whether learning about microbes is fun. Fun, quantified. Play, studied.
arxiv-2606-17055: Dantong Niu and colleagues present T-Rex, a robotic hand that reacts to touch. arxiv-2606-16955: Combinatorialists Matías Azócar Carvajal, Ayush Basu, Christian Reiher, and collaborators prove a canonical Ramsey theorem for graphs whose intersections are clean. arxiv-2606-17155: Kuldeep Deka studies how dark matter could have been born during reheating, the cosmic epoch when the universe's first furnace relit after inflation. arxiv-2606-17355: Sharva Gogawale and colleagues classify complex document layouts in the wild with little training data. arxiv-2606-17455: Changseob Song and Inseung Kang personalize exoskeleton control continuously online with manifold-aware experience replay. arxiv-2606-17755: Pierre-Louis Curien and colleagues build tridendriform algebras on hypergraph polytopes, approaching the construction from the other direction. arxiv-2606-18055: Steven Seeger and colleagues characterize the MERMAID-v1 PET scanner prototype, including its first zebrafish scans. arxiv-2606-18155: Laura Rueda-Nieto and colleagues use X-ray eclipse tomography to resolve the extent of X-ray-emitting regions in a Seyfert galaxy. arxiv-2606-18355: Rena Lee and colleagues revisit the exo-Mercury candidate GJ 367 b with ESPRESSO and a self-consistent tidal distortion model. arxiv-2606-18455: Amogh Srivastav and colleagues compress the CMB likelihood for dark energy, curvature, and massive neutrinos with CMBComp. plos-pone-0003455: Infection researchers explained why flesh-eating strep beats the immune system in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003555: Bioinformaticians proved different machines can agree in this 2008 methods paper. plos-pone-0003655: In 2008, Griguer, Oliva, and Gobin reframed a brain-tumor marker. plos-pone-0003755: In 2008, Ospina, Seida, and Clark sifted the evidence on autism therapies. Their systematic review asked which behavioral and developmental interventions truly ease core autism symptoms. The careful sorting separates supported approaches from hype in a field full of claims.
plos-pone-0003855: A 2008 cell biology paper gave a centriole protein its job description. Mikael Le Clech showed CAP350 keeps centriolar tubules stable and helps assemble centrioles, the cell's organizing centers. The finding fills in how these nine-triplet cylinders get built right.
plos-pone-0003955: In 2008, Epstein, Parker, and Cummings modeled fear spreading alongside disease. Their math coupled contagion dynamics of panic with those of pathogens. The dual-spread model shows epidemics of fear can outrun the germs themselves.
plos-pone-0004055: In 2008, Capra, Skrovanek, and Kruglyak compared two worm strains growing up. They profiled gene expression across development in two C. elegans isolates. plos-pone-0004255: In 2009, a team found ghost skins after cell division. Nuclear envelope scraps proved fluid and rich in sterols. The leftover sheets carried rare lipid signals too. The find reframes what survives mitosis. The skins may seed the next nuclear envelope.

plos-pone-0004555: In 2009, Mutoh, Perron, and Dimitrov compared three glowing voltage sensors. Spectrally-resolved properties of three FRET-based fluorescent protein voltage sensors were measured. plos-pone-0004655: In 2009, Mendonsa, Dobrowolska, and Lin profiled key stress signals in Alzheimer's brains. Stress signal chains in Alzheimer's were charted. The fresh-look approach was tested head-on. The study helps future care design a lot. The heavy social cost is growing fast.

plos-pone-0348455: Controlling how fast proteins get made could unlock biology in neglected species. plos-pone-0358555: Eliminating measles and rubella is a long, grinding campaign. This paper tracked Lesotho’s progress toward elimination from 2011 to 2025. The fourteen-year record shows how far the small kingdom has come — and what still stands in the way of zero cases.
plos-pone-0358455: Erythropoietin — the blood-boosting hormone — may also signal eye damage in diabetes. plos-pone-0357755: Childhood leukemia evolves in stages — and mathematics can track its moves. plos-pone-0350955: Alcohol use disorder impairs executive function — but how severely, and does it predict who recovers? plos-pone-0356255: Women and mothers carry an invisible mental load — the endless background planning nobody sees. plos-pone-0355855: The antimicrobial peptide LL-37, better known for fighting germs, may also mark sleep quality. plos-pone-0355955: Exosomes — tiny vesicles — secreted by brown versus white fat cells carry strikingly different messages. plos-pone-0357355: This entry is a correction notice, not a research finding. It amends the paper characterizing an AGAMOUS-like MADS box protein — a probable regulator of flowering and fruit ripening in banana. Readers should consult the corrected version for the accurate scientific record.

plos-pone-0349155: Antiphospholipid syndrome — a clotting disorder — may yield to new drug targets. plos-pone-0356955: This entry is an Expression of Concern, not a research finding. The journal has flagged the paper on constipation in Tg2576 Alzheimer’s mice, linked to dysregulation involving mAChR signaling pathways. The notice alerts readers that the paper’s reliability is under investigation.
plos-pone-0356055: Spatial neglect after stroke — ignoring half the world — resists conventional therapy. plos-pone-0354855: Acute rheumatic fever still damages young hearts — and future doctors must recognize it. This paper evaluated medical students’ awareness of the disease. The awareness gaps it found point to curriculum fixes that could save children from preventable heart damage.
plos-pone-0352555: Can AI design vocational curricula — and would anyone trust the results? plos-pone-0355655: This entry is a retraction notice, not a research finding. plos-pone-0354755: Neotropical bats — from nectar-sippers to fruit-gorgers — process sugar in remarkably varied ways. plos-pone-0355055: For ventilated patients with tracheostomies, when to deflate the cuff matters. This observational study investigated cuff deflation timing in prolonged mechanical ventilation. plos-pone-0353755: When home becomes a dangerous place — falls among community-dwelling elders — the costs cascade. This paper quantified the cost of falls among older people living at home. plos-pone-0354455: Power grid maintenance workers face scenario-specific occupational risks. This paper conducted scenario-based risk assessment for them. The structured assessment gives utilities the foresight to protect the workers who keep the lights on — often at great personal risk.
plos-pone-0353955: Cerebellar damage impairs social prediction — reading others’ intentions. plos-pone-0354355: Young couples divorcing in Western Iran — their own explanations were never systematically heard. plos-pone-0353355: Patients asking AI about knee osteoarthritis — how good are the answers? plos-pone-0354255: Tan Twan Eng’s The Garden of Evening Mists — personality and emotion encoded linguistically. This systemic functional discourse analysis examined those realizations. The findings reveal how a master novelist builds character through grammar — linguistics meeting literary art.

plos-pone-0353655: Young rural-to-urban Chinese migrants — ethnic self-identity’s impact on social integration. This interpretative phenomenological analysis examined it. plos-pone-0352855: Mountainous curve car-following — modeled with driving behavior characteristics. This paper built that model. The findings captured how drivers adapt to winding ascents. The research served autonomous vehicles — teaching machines the mountain driver’s art.
plos-pone-0339255: Urinary tract infections in Indonesia — diagnosed clinically — need faster, better confirmation. plos-pone-0352755: Yellow fever — its immunoprevention and immunomodulation — scoped across global and Latin American evidence. This review synthesized it. plos-pone-0350655: AI-generated images — detected via adversarial perturbation-induced reconstruction discrepancy. ADRD is that detector. The method exposed diffusion models’ fingerprints. The findings armed the fight against synthetic media — truth’s technical defense.
plos-pone-0353555: Vertebrate mitochondrial control regions — their evolutionary patterns in large-scale comparative analysis. This paper did so. plos-pone-0352155: Water resource carrying capacity — assessed by an intuitionistic fuzzy PAMSSEM method with cumulative prospect theory for multi-attribute group decision-making. plos-pone-0353155: Large language models — their performance in Risk of Bias assessments, validated cross-sectionally. This paper evaluated it. The findings tested whether AI can judge study quality. plos-pone-0352455: Ugandan malaria vector control — combined intervention strategies reviewed from two districts’ secondary data. This paper did so. The findings compared the combinations. plos-pone-0339755: Blood pressure scaling during sleep — short- and long-term, with pulse arrival time, in healthy controls and sleep apnea patients. This paper studied the behavior. plos-pone-0351955: Pesticide-spiked perilla and broccoli — residue removal efficiency with microplasma-treated water. This paper measured it. The analysis tested the activated water’s cleaning power. plos-pone-0352255: Kathmandu young adults with grade C periodontitis — tooth loss and associated factors during maintenance care. This paper studied them. The analysis tracked the teeth lost despite care. Its dental value is the prognosis. The work counts the teeth that couldn’t be saved.
plos-pone-0335155: Romanian construction workers — workplace changes, perceived difficulties, and migration intentions during COVID-19. This paper studied them. plos-pone-0352355: Advanced glycation end products — accumulated through mitochondrial oxidative stress. This paper demonstrated the promotion. plos-pone-0340955: Advanced HIV rapid tests by Malawian lay providers — high performance in a prospective diagnostic accuracy study. This paper showed it. The analysis validated the task-shifting. europmc-pmc2811155: Damaged mitochondria must be cleared before they poison the cell, and this 2010 paper reveals a key alarm system. europmc-pmc2815955: Nipah virus kept spilling from bats into people in Bangladesh, and this 2009 paper documents the pattern.
